summary: Cross-project contracts, phase 1: the consumer-side declaration format and its parser, shipped INERT. New scripts/phasekit-contracts.py defines the conventions as a single source of truth (contracts.yaml at the repo root, vendor/contracts/<slug>/ for vendored copies, /contracts + index.json for the provider mount, PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR to override it) and exposes load_declaration() plus a `status` subcommand. Nothing mounts and nothing refuses yet. The parser is deliberately strict — unknown top-level or entry keys, a wrong version, a slug with a path separator, an absolute/traversal vendor path and duplicate slugs are all hard errors — because a typo'd key that silently does nothing is the exact bug class this release exists to kill. Registered under scripts: in capabilities/project-capabilities.yaml and in ALWAYS_INSTALLED_FILE_PATHS so it provisions downstream.
decision_memo: foundry-meta/KICKOFF-phasekit-v070-contracts.md + DESIGN-cross-project-contracts.md (approved 2026-08-16; forks A/B/C and the standalone amendment already decided — phase 1 re-litigated nothing)
reviewer_notes: Audit first: grepped the tree for existing contracts machinery — none existed. Greenfield, no rewrite risk.
Deliberately did NOT start from the earliest unapproved entry in docs/META_PHASES.md; the kickoff overrides that for this release (M9.x is unrelated work and would never reach contracts).

Ownership class: contracts.yaml is PROJECT-owned and is NOT registered as an installed file, so `phasekit upgrade` can never erase a project's declarations. Only the reader script ships. A regression test pinning upgrade-preservation lands with the gate in phase 3.

Bare-string shorthand (`depends_on: [slug]`) is accepted alongside the mapping form and normalizes to one internal representation. Two spellings, one meaning — chosen because an agent authoring the file is likely to reach for the simple form, and a rejected-but-obvious spelling is a failure mode, not a safeguard.

The gate must live in a phasekit-owned script rather than only in the project-owned scripts/phasekit-verify.sh: a check the policed repo can edit away is not a check. Recorded in the capabilities entry so the reason survives the commit.

deferred_items.description: Mount plumbing: container-setup.sh accepts a provider-supplied contracts path and bind-mounts it read-only at /contracts; index.json is read and honoured, including the zero-entry case.
The gate: vendored == mounted equality pin, refusal when the repo declares dependencies and no provider is present, and a one-command refresh named by exact command in the failure message.
Session-prompt awareness, stack-profile seeding, docs, capability registration review, tag and push v0.7.0.
